druid-lake.name: Druid Lake
druid-lake.description: Druid Lake is the park's reservoir landscape and the focus of a reopened walking and rolling loop; it is scenery and recreation space, not a swimming lake.
druid-lake.address: 900 Druid Park Lake Drive, Baltimore, MD 21217
druid-lake.sourceLabel: Baltimore City Department of Public Works
druid-lake.location: Use the lake-loop access along Druid Park Lake Drive rather than the park's general pin. The modified continuous loop reopened in May 2025 after the underground tank project; fencing and signed restoration areas still control where visitors may go.
druid-lake.parking: Legal curb and park parking varies around the lake. Do not stop in the Big Jump lane or against construction barriers, and follow temporary event, restoration, and street-parking signs.
druid-lake.hours: Use the lake loop during ordinary daylight park hours. Construction, major events, storms, ice, maintenance, and temporary safety work can close or redirect parts of the route independently.
druid-lake.restrooms: There is no dependable restroom directly on the lake loop. Plan around staffed destinations such as Rawlings Conservatory or the Maryland Zoo during their own open hours, and do not assume those facilities admit non-ticketed restroom visits.
druid-lake.fees: Walking and rolling around Druid Lake is free. Nearby staffed attractions, programs, parking restrictions, and reserved events are separate.
druid-lake.accessibility: The reopened loop is paved, but temporary fencing, crossings, grades, construction transitions, and the park's surrounding high-speed roads can affect a step-free trip. Use current signs and the protected Big Jump connection where it serves the route.
druid-lake.dogs: Leashed dogs may use ordinary outdoor park routes. Keep them out of the lake and restoration areas, yield on the shared path, and remove waste.
druid-lake.family: The loop is a practical stroller, walking, and bicycling objective when weather and construction are calm. Keep children beside an adult at road crossings and barriers, and do not treat the lake edge as a swimming or play-water area.
druid-lake.need: The loop is open, but the landscape has changed from its pre-construction form. Follow current fencing rather than old maps, and check Baltimore City notices before a trip built around uninterrupted access.

howard-peters-rawlings-conservatory.name: Howard Peters Rawlings Conservatory
howard-peters-rawlings-conservatory.description: The historic glasshouse and five greenhouse environments are a separately staffed destination inside Druid Hill Park with much shorter hours than the surrounding grounds.
howard-peters-rawlings-conservatory.location: Enter Druid Hill Park from Gwynns Falls Parkway, turn right after entering, and follow signs to 3100 Swann Drive. The conservatory is near McCulloh Street and Gwynns Falls Parkway, not beside the zoo entrance.
howard-peters-rawlings-conservatory.parking: The conservatory documents ample free parking nearby inside Druid Hill Park. Vehicle access can be suspended for major events, so read the same-day notice before driving into the park.
howard-peters-rawlings-conservatory.hours: Open Wednesday-Friday 11 a.m.-3 p.m. and Saturday-Sunday 10 a.m.-4 p.m.; closed Monday, Tuesday, Thanksgiving, and Christmas. The official visit page also lists full vehicle closure for AFRAM June 19-21, 2026 and a conservatory closure for the Caribbean Fest parade July 11, 2026.
howard-peters-rawlings-conservatory.restrooms: Use the conservatory's visitor facilities during staffed hours. Do not rely on building access before opening, after closing, or during an event closure.
howard-peters-rawlings-conservatory.fees: The official visit page offers advance donation and ticket options. Check the current ticket page rather than relying on an older admission amount.
howard-peters-rawlings-conservatory.accessibility: Use the nearby parking and main visitor entrance for the shortest paved approach. Historic greenhouse aisles and event layouts can vary; contact the conservatory for a specific accommodation or group need.
howard-peters-rawlings-conservatory.dogs: Pets are not a normal fit inside the conservatory. Qualified service animals should be confirmed under current visitor rules; ordinary park dog rules resume outside the staffed facility.
howard-peters-rawlings-conservatory.family: The compact greenhouse environments work well as a weather-aware family stop, but adults should confirm the limited open days and supervise children around plants, glass, water, and narrow visitor aisles.
howard-peters-rawlings-conservatory.need: Do not plan around general park hours. The conservatory is closed Monday and Tuesday, keeps short daytime hours, and posts event-related vehicle and building closures separately.

maryland-zoo-in-baltimore.name: Maryland Zoo in Baltimore
maryland-zoo-in-baltimore.description: The Maryland Zoo is a ticketed, separately operated outdoor attraction within Druid Hill Park, with its own gate, parking, rules, food, restrooms, and daily operating schedule.
maryland-zoo-in-baltimore.location: Navigate to One Safari Place and the Maryland Zoo front gate, not the Druid Hill Park or Rawlings Conservatory pin. Use the zoo's current map after entering because exhibits and animal visibility can change during the day.
maryland-zoo-in-baltimore.parking: Use zoo-designated parking at the front-gate arrival. Free accessible spaces are to the left of the front gate on a first-come basis; event traffic elsewhere in Druid Hill Park can alter the approach.
maryland-zoo-in-baltimore.hours: The zoo publishes daily hours and alerts on its own site; the page checked August 10, 2026 showed 10 a.m.-4 p.m. Confirm the selected date because seasonal hours, events, weather, and animal operations can differ.
maryland-zoo-in-baltimore.restrooms: Accessible restrooms with baby-changing stations are distributed through the zoo. Family restrooms are documented near Whistle Stop Grille and inside the Penguin Education Center.
maryland-zoo-in-baltimore.fees: Zoo admission is ticketed and separate from free general park access. Use the official ticket page for current date-based admission, memberships, rentals, and paid experiences.
maryland-zoo-in-baltimore.accessibility: The zoo provides first-come accessible parking, accessible restrooms, ADA-compliant shuttles, and first-come wheelchair, ECV, and stroller rentals. Druid Hill topography and some animal areas create route or device limitations, so review the current accessibility page.
maryland-zoo-in-baltimore.dogs: Pets are not permitted anywhere on zoo grounds, including parking lots. ADA-defined service animals are permitted under the zoo's service-animal rules.
maryland-zoo-in-baltimore.family: The zoo is designed for family visits, but adults must supervise children, stay on marked paths, respect barriers, and accept that animals may choose off-exhibit areas.
maryland-zoo-in-baltimore.need: This is an outdoor, ticketed visit: the zoo says rain checks and refunds are not issued. Check weather, daily alerts, tickets, and the day's schedule before crossing the park.

chinese-pavilion.name: Chinese Pavilion
chinese-pavilion.description: The Chinese Pavilion is a distinctive open-air landmark on Swann Drive, useful as a precise meeting point and a short historic-landscape stop within the much larger park.
chinese-pavilion.address: Swann Drive, Druid Hill Park, Baltimore, MD 21217
chinese-pavilion.sourceLabel: Baltimore City Recreation and Parks master plan
chinese-pavilion.location: Use the geotagged pavilion point on Swann Drive. It is south of the conservatory and lake-side attractions, so the general Druid Hill Park pin is not a reliable walking destination.
chinese-pavilion.parking: Use an open legal park space serving Swann Drive and walk the final approach. Do not park on grass, block the pavilion, or assume a nearby event or maintenance lane is visitor parking.
chinese-pavilion.hours: The open-air pavilion follows ordinary daylight park access unless a permit, event, maintenance project, or posted closure controls the area.
chinese-pavilion.restrooms: There is no documented dependable restroom at the pavilion. Use a staffed destination during its own operating hours before walking to this landmark.
chinese-pavilion.fees: Casual outdoor viewing is free. Reserved or organized use may require a city permit.
chinese-pavilion.accessibility: The pavilion is beside a park drive and lawn setting, but curb, grade, surface, and event conditions vary. Review the final approach on arrival rather than assuming every side is step-free.
chinese-pavilion.dogs: Leashed dogs may accompany visitors in ordinary outdoor park space. Keep them out of permitted gatherings and remove waste.
chinese-pavilion.family: This is a short visual landmark rather than a staffed attraction. Children should stay with an adult around the road, steps, railings, and any event setup.
chinese-pavilion.need: There is no admission desk or guaranteed facility service here. Treat it as an outdoor landmark and pair it with another destination only after checking walking distance and current park access.

mansion-house-lawn.name: Mansion House Lawn
mansion-house-lawn.description: Mansion House Lawn is a broad historic open landscape near the zoo side of Druid Hill Park, suited to walking, informal recreation, and understanding the scale of the original estate grounds.
mansion-house-lawn.address: Mansion House Drive, Druid Hill Park, Baltimore, MD 21217
mansion-house-lawn.sourceLabel: Baltimore City Recreation and Parks master plan
mansion-house-lawn.location: Navigate to the mapped lawn on Mansion House Drive rather than to Druid Lake or Rawlings Conservatory. The photographed lawn is an open landscape, not the zoo's ticket entrance.
mansion-house-lawn.parking: Use a legal open space serving Mansion House Drive or the selected nearby attraction. Zoo parking and access rules apply if the trip enters zoo property; do not cross a closed gate or use service roads as shortcuts.
mansion-house-lawn.hours: The outdoor lawn follows daylight park access unless an event permit, zoo operation, maintenance activity, or posted closure restricts it.
mansion-house-lawn.restrooms: There is no guaranteed restroom on the lawn. Nearby zoo restrooms are inside the ticketed attraction, so plan restroom access before settling into this area.
mansion-house-lawn.fees: Casual access to ordinary park lawn is free. Zoo admission, permitted events, programs, and reservations are separate.
mansion-house-lawn.accessibility: Roadside and paved approaches exist, while the lawn itself is grass with natural grades and weather-sensitive footing. Use the nearest legal arrival point for a shorter firm-surface approach.
mansion-house-lawn.dogs: Leashed dogs may use ordinary outdoor park areas but may not enter Maryland Zoo grounds. Keep dogs clear of organized activities and remove waste.
mansion-house-lawn.family: The open lawn offers room to pause and move, but it has no dedicated staffed family facilities. Maintain supervision near roads and confirm whether an event controls the space.
mansion-house-lawn.need: The lawn and zoo are adjacent but not interchangeable. A lawn visit does not include zoo entry, restrooms, or parking privileges, and permitted events can temporarily change access.

patterson-park-observatory.name: Patterson Park Observatory
patterson-park-observatory.description: The 1891-92 Observatory, widely called the Pagoda, is Patterson Park's signature hilltop landmark and viewpoint, but its interior is currently closed for maintenance indefinitely.
patterson-park-observatory.location: Use the mapped Observatory point near the west side of the park. Approach on park paths from the Baltimore Street, Pratt Street, or Patterson Park Avenue side rather than navigating to the pool on Linwood Avenue.
patterson-park-observatory.parking: There is no general visitor parking inside Patterson Park. Use legal perimeter street parking, read residential restrictions, and leave permitted and emergency vehicle routes clear.
patterson-park-observatory.hours: The exterior grounds follow dawn-to-dusk park hours. Although older schedules describe seasonal Sunday interior hours, the current landmarks page says the Observatory is closed for maintenance indefinitely; do not promise tower entry.
patterson-park-observatory.restrooms: There is no dependable public restroom inside the Observatory while it is closed. Plan around an open staffed park facility and verify access before walking uphill.
patterson-park-observatory.fees: Viewing the exterior and surrounding park is free. There is no current paid admission that overrides the indefinite interior closure.
patterson-park-observatory.accessibility: Paved park paths reach the hill area, but grades and the historic tower interior require separate consideration. The closed interior should not be treated as an available accessible viewpoint.
patterson-park-observatory.dogs: Leashed dogs may use surrounding park paths under the six-foot leash rule. Keep dogs outside the structure and away from gardens or posted event areas.
patterson-park-observatory.family: The exterior is a memorable family landmark and city-view stop, but adults should prepare children for a closed tower and supervise them on the hill, steps, and paths.
patterson-park-observatory.need: Current closure overrides the usual seasonal Sunday schedule. Visit for the exterior, gardens, and hilltop setting, and recheck the official landmarks page before expecting interior access.

boat-lake.name: Boat Lake
boat-lake.description: Boat Lake is Patterson Park's restored wetland and open-water habitat, now used for fishing, wildlife viewing, and education rather than public boating or swimming.
boat-lake.address: Patterson Park near Eastern Avenue and South Milton Avenue, Baltimore, MD 21224
boat-lake.location: The lake lies in the southern part of the park near Eastern Avenue and Milton Avenue. Use the mapped lake point and park paths; the Baltimore Street recreation-center address is on the opposite side of the park.
boat-lake.parking: Use legal perimeter street parking near Eastern Avenue or adjacent side streets, then walk in. Unauthorized private vehicles are not allowed on park paths.
boat-lake.hours: The outdoor lake area follows dawn-to-dusk park hours. Ice, storms, maintenance, habitat work, fishing restrictions, and events can change practical access.
boat-lake.restrooms: There is no dependable restroom at the shoreline. Use a staffed seasonal or recreation facility only when it is open, and plan for a walk across the park.
boat-lake.fees: Wildlife viewing and ordinary park access are free. Fishing rules and any required Maryland license still apply.
boat-lake.accessibility: Primary park approaches are paved, but shoreline edges, grass, wet surfaces, and habitat areas are not uniform. Stay on established paths and use the closest Eastern Avenue-side entrance.
boat-lake.dogs: Dogs must remain leashed at six feet or less outside the dog park. Keep dogs out of the water and wetland plantings and away from wildlife.
boat-lake.family: The lake is useful for birds, fish, and nature observation, but it is not a splash pad, swimming area, or boating attraction. Keep children beside an adult at the water edge.
boat-lake.need: The historic name can mislead visitors: current official guidance describes fishing, wildlife viewing, and education, not public boat rental or swimming.

marble-fountain.name: Marble Fountain
marble-fountain.description: The restored 1865 Marble Fountain is a small gathering landmark near the Lombard Street and Patterson Park Avenue side of the park.
marble-fountain.address: Patterson Park near East Lombard Street and South Patterson Park Avenue, Baltimore, MD 21231
marble-fountain.location: Use the destination's geotagged point near East Lombard Street and South Patterson Park Avenue. It is west of Boat Lake and far from the Linwood Avenue pool and rink.
marble-fountain.parking: Use legal perimeter street parking near Lombard Street or Patterson Park Avenue and walk in. Read neighborhood restrictions and do not drive onto park paths.
marble-fountain.hours: The outdoor fountain area follows dawn-to-dusk park hours. Water operation can be seasonal or interrupted by weather and maintenance, so the landmark may be visible without flowing.
marble-fountain.restrooms: There is no documented dependable restroom at the fountain. Verify an open staffed park facility before relying on restroom access.
marble-fountain.fees: Viewing the fountain is free. Permitted events held around it may control the immediate space.
marble-fountain.accessibility: The fountain is reached by paved park paths, while curb cuts, grades, temporary event barriers, and fountain-edge conditions can vary by approach.
marble-fountain.dogs: Leashed dogs may use surrounding paths under the six-foot leash rule. Keep them out of the basin and remove waste.
marble-fountain.family: The fountain makes a short visual stop, but the basin is not a splash pad. Children should remain outside the railing and with an adult.
marble-fountain.need: Do not make water flow the sole reason for the trip. Seasonal shutdown, maintenance, or an event can leave the fountain off or the immediate plaza occupied.

war-of-1812-memorial-cannons.name: War of 1812 Memorial Cannons
war-of-1812-memorial-cannons.description: The memorial cannons sit beside the Observatory area and recall Patterson Park's role at Hampstead Hill during the defense of Baltimore.
war-of-1812-memorial-cannons.address: Patterson Park near the Observatory, Baltimore, MD 21224
war-of-1812-memorial-cannons.location: Use the geotagged cannon point by the Observatory rather than searching the athletic-field or pool side of the park. The two landmarks can be visited in one short hilltop circuit.
war-of-1812-memorial-cannons.parking: Use legal perimeter street parking and walk to the Observatory hill. No general visitor vehicles are allowed on park paths.
war-of-1812-memorial-cannons.hours: The outdoor memorial follows dawn-to-dusk park access unless maintenance, a permitted event, or a posted closure controls the hilltop area.
war-of-1812-memorial-cannons.restrooms: There is no restroom at the cannons. The nearby Observatory interior is closed indefinitely and should not be counted as a restroom stop.
war-of-1812-memorial-cannons.fees: The outdoor memorial is free to view.
war-of-1812-memorial-cannons.accessibility: Paved park paths approach the hill, but grade and the immediate landscape should be assessed for the chosen mobility need. The cannons are historic objects, not play equipment.
war-of-1812-memorial-cannons.dogs: Leashed dogs may use surrounding paths under the six-foot leash rule. Keep animals off the memorial base and gardens.
war-of-1812-memorial-cannons.family: This is a compact history stop that pairs naturally with the Observatory exterior. Children should not climb or sit on the cannons and should stay with an adult on the hill.
war-of-1812-memorial-cannons.need: The site is unstaffed and has no interpretive desk or guaranteed facilities. Read the memorial in place, protect the historic objects, and plan restroom access elsewhere.

virginia-s-baker-recreation-center.name: Virginia S. Baker Recreation Center
virginia-s-baker-recreation-center.description: Virginia S. Baker Recreation Center is Patterson Park's year-round indoor program hub, with a gym, multipurpose and meeting rooms, game room, kitchen, and computer lab.
virginia-s-baker-recreation-center.location: The center is inside the north side of the park near East Baltimore Street and Luzerne Avenue. Use 2601 East Baltimore Street rather than the southern pool, rink, or Boat Lake entrances.
virginia-s-baker-recreation-center.parking: Use legal perimeter street parking near Baltimore Street and walk to the center. There is no general visitor parking inside Patterson Park, and program or event demand can tighten nearby availability.
virginia-s-baker-recreation-center.hours: The center has year-round programming but does not share dawn-to-dusk park hours. Call 410-396-9156 or check the current city program schedule before expecting the building, gym, or a specific activity to be open.
virginia-s-baker-recreation-center.restrooms: Restroom access is tied to the recreation center being open for programs. Do not rely on indoor access outside current staffed hours.
virginia-s-baker-recreation-center.fees: Building entry and program costs vary by activity. Confirm the current city schedule, registration, age rules, and any fee before arriving.
virginia-s-baker-recreation-center.accessibility: Use the recreation-center entrance and exact city facility pin for the shortest approach. Contact the center for a program-specific accommodation or to confirm room and entrance access.
virginia-s-baker-recreation-center.dogs: Pets are not a normal fit inside the recreation center. ADA-defined service animals follow applicable facility rules; park leash rules apply outside.
virginia-s-baker-recreation-center.family: The center supports youth and adult programs year-round, but drop-in availability cannot be inferred from the park being open. Confirm the exact activity, age range, and registration first.
virginia-s-baker-recreation-center.need: This is a scheduled, staffed facility rather than an always-open park amenity. Call or check the current program listing before crossing the park for indoor access.

federal-hill-harbor-overlook.name: Federal Hill Harbor Overlook
federal-hill-harbor-overlook.description: The Federal Hill Harbor Overlook is the park's photographed northwest-facing slope and upper-rim viewpoint across Baltimore's Inner Harbor and downtown skyline.
federal-hill-harbor-overlook.address: Federal Hill Park, Warren Avenue, Baltimore, MD 21230
federal-hill-harbor-overlook.location: Use the geotagged viewpoint on the northwest slope below the upper rim, then walk the nearby paved edge for alternate skyline angles. It is west of the playground and not the lower basketball court.
federal-hill-harbor-overlook.parking: There is no dedicated overlook lot. Read current street signs around Warren, Battery and Covington or use a paid Inner Harbor garage; weekend and event demand can be intense.
federal-hill-harbor-overlook.hours: Baltimore's official general park guidance says parks are open dawn to dusk. Events, maintenance, ice or posted restrictions can change access to an individual path or slope.
federal-hill-harbor-overlook.restrooms: There is no dependable public restroom at the overlook. Use an open Inner Harbor visitor facility, museum or business before climbing.
federal-hill-harbor-overlook.fees: The overlook and ordinary park access are free. Street meters, garages, nearby attractions, permits and special events are separate.
federal-hill-harbor-overlook.accessibility: The upper plateau is the easier approach, but the exact photographed slope point is below the rim and may require a grade. Visitors avoiding stairs should approach from Warren Avenue and choose a paved upper-rim view.
federal-hill-harbor-overlook.dogs: Leashed dogs may accompany visitors on ordinary park paths. Keep them controlled near slopes, walls, children and busy bordering streets, and remove waste.
federal-hill-harbor-overlook.family: The skyline view is a quick family stop that pairs naturally with the fenced hilltop playground. Supervise closely near walls, steep grass and the harbor-side stairs.
federal-hill-harbor-overlook.need: The geotag marks one strong photographed angle, not the only viewpoint. Wind, glare and afternoon storms can change the experience quickly on the exposed hill.

fort-mchenry-visitor-center.name: Paul S. Sarbanes Visitor and Education Center
fort-mchenry-visitor-center.description: The Paul S. Sarbanes Visitor and Education Center is the free orientation hub for Fort McHenry, with the film, museum, ranger desk, bookstore, restrooms and Star Fort pass sales.
fort-mchenry-visitor-center.location: Follow the park road from East Fort Avenue to the main parking lot. The Visitor and Education Center is directly beside the lot and should be the first stop before walking toward the historic zone.
fort-mchenry-visitor-center.parking: Free main and overflow parking, including first-come accessible spaces, serves the center. Parking is for park visitors and fills more quickly during major programs.
fort-mchenry-visitor-center.hours: Current summer hours are 9:00 a.m.-4:45 p.m. Monday-Friday and 9:00 a.m.-5:45 p.m. Saturday-Sunday. Seasonal hours and Thanksgiving, December 25 and January 1 closures apply; recheck NPS before leaving.
fort-mchenry-visitor-center.restrooms: Accessible and family restrooms, bottle-filling and drinking water are inside. Exterior vending machines offer snacks and drinks, but access follows building hours.
fort-mchenry-visitor-center.fees: The visitor center, exhibits and orientation film are free. Star Fort Historic Zone admission is sold separately at the front desk and is currently $15 per adult age 16 and older.
fort-mchenry-visitor-center.accessibility: The building, parking, restrooms, film and exhibits are accessible; wheelchairs can be borrowed, the film is captioned and exhibits include audio narration. Request ASL interpretation at least 14 days ahead.
fort-mchenry-visitor-center.dogs: Pets are not allowed inside the building, even in carriers. ADA-defined service animals are permitted; leashed pets may use designated outdoor grounds.
fort-mchenry-visitor-center.family: Pick up Junior Ranger booklets, see the ten-minute film and ask the ranger desk about same-day programs before walking to the fort. Baby-changing and family-restroom facilities are available.
fort-mchenry-visitor-center.need: Pass registers close before the building and park gates. Buy Star Fort admission early and confirm the final film and program times at the desk.

star-fort.name: Star Fort
star-fort.description: The historic Star Fort is Fort McHenry's paid interior zone, preserving original brick, bastions, barracks and exhibits spanning the War of 1812 through World War I.
star-fort.location: Start at the Visitor and Education Center to buy or validate admission, then follow the paved path east to the fenced historic zone and Star Fort entrance.
star-fort.parking: Use the free main visitor lot by the Visitor Center, not service roads near the fort. The walk to the historic zone is part of the visit.
star-fort.hours: The Star Fort opens at 9:00 a.m. and closes 15 minutes before the park gates. Summer closing is 4:45 p.m. weekdays and 5:45 p.m. weekends; seasonal and holiday schedules apply.
star-fort.restrooms: Accessible restrooms are available inside the Star Fort during historic-zone hours and at the Visitor Center. Do not count on access after the zone closes.
star-fort.fees: Admission is currently $15 per adult age 16 and older; children 15 and younger enter free. The pass is valid for seven days, the site is cashless and federal passes are accepted.
star-fort.accessibility: A paved route reaches the fort and most interior exhibits are accessible, but historic surfaces and individual rooms vary. Borrow a wheelchair or ask the Visitor Center about a specific route.
star-fort.dogs: Pets are prohibited within the split-rail-fenced Historic Zone and Star Fort. ADA-defined service animals are permitted.
star-fort.family: The fort, exhibits, ranger interpretation and Junior Ranger activities are the core family history experience. Keep children off walls and artifacts and allow time for the orientation film first.
star-fort.need: The free grounds and the paid Star Fort are different experiences. Arrive early enough to buy admission and complete the interior before its earlier closing time.

fort-mchenry-seawall-trail.name: Fort McHenry Seawall Trail
fort-mchenry-seawall-trail.description: The Fort McHenry Seawall Trail is a free paved one-mile loop connecting the Visitor Center area with Patapsco River views, benches, cherry trees, interpretive signs and Orpheus.
fort-mchenry-seawall-trail.location: This pin marks the named paved trail segment beside the Visitor Center. Follow the signed loop around the park rather than navigating to a single waterfront photo point.
fort-mchenry-seawall-trail.parking: Use the free main or overflow visitor lot and join the trail near the Visitor Center. Do not park on service roads or assume the lot remains open after park gates close.
fort-mchenry-seawall-trail.hours: The trail follows park-ground hours: summer 7:00 a.m.-5:00 p.m. weekdays and 7:00 a.m.-6:00 p.m. weekends, with shorter seasonal hours. All visitors must exit before gates close.
fort-mchenry-seawall-trail.restrooms: Use accessible restrooms at the Visitor Center or Star Fort while those buildings are open. There are no continuously open facilities around the waterfront loop.
fort-mchenry-seawall-trail.fees: The Seawall Trail is free; a Star Fort ticket is not required. Parking is also free for park visitors.
fort-mchenry-seawall-trail.accessibility: NPS identifies the paved trail as wheelchair accessible and lists benches along the route. Wind, debris, snow, ice or temporary work can still affect an individual segment.
fort-mchenry-seawall-trail.dogs: Leashed pets are allowed on the trail with a leash no longer than six feet. Bring waste bags, keep pets away from wildlife and remember that pets cannot enter the historic zone or buildings.
fort-mchenry-seawall-trail.family: The flat loop offers a lower-cost, flexible family visit with harbor views and room to walk, run or bike. Bring water and keep children away from the seawall edge and roadway crossings.
fort-mchenry-seawall-trail.need: The route is about one mile, with roughly three-quarters of a mile along the river. Harbor wind and limited shade can make it feel longer in heat or cold.

orpheus-statue.name: Orpheus Statue
orpheus-statue.description: Orpheus with the Awkward Foot is the large 1922 Francis Scott Key monument beside the west side of Fort McHenry's Seawall Trail.
orpheus-statue.location: Use the exact named OpenStreetMap artwork pin on the west side of the park. The monument sits along the Seawall Trail, west of the Star Fort and southwest of the main parking area.
orpheus-statue.parking: Park in the free main visitor lot and walk the Seawall Trail to the monument. There is no separate monument parking, and nearby roads are not visitor spaces.
orpheus-statue.hours: The outdoor monument follows park-ground hours and gate closures. It does not share the Star Fort admission requirement or interior closing line.
orpheus-statue.restrooms: There are no restrooms at the statue. Use the Visitor Center or Star Fort facilities while those buildings are open.
orpheus-statue.fees: Viewing Orpheus and walking the surrounding trail are free. Star Fort admission is separate.
orpheus-statue.accessibility: The monument is reached from the paved, wheelchair-accessible Seawall Trail. The final viewing angle and nearby lawn may have grades or grass.
orpheus-statue.dogs: Leashed pets may visit the outdoor monument and trail. Keep the leash within six feet, remove waste and do not continue into pet-restricted historic or building areas.
orpheus-statue.family: Orpheus is an easy visual landmark on a short trail segment, but there is no staffed interpretation or play equipment at the statue itself.
orpheus-statue.need: The monument is commonly described as Orpheus, while its mapped full name is Orpheus with the Awkward Foot. Save the exact pin because it is outside the Star Fort interior.

cylburn-mansion.name: Cylburn Mansion
cylburn-mansion.description: Cylburn Mansion is the arboretum's 1863 stone centerpiece, with public interior access limited to a seasonal building schedule rather than the full grounds day.
cylburn-mansion.location: Follow the paved internal route north from the main parking area to the named Mansion building. It is beyond the Vollmer Center circle and should not be confused with the Nature Education Center or Greenhouse Classroom.
cylburn-mansion.parking: Use free arboretum parking near the main entrance and Vollmer Center, then walk to the Mansion. Accessible spaces are in the upper lot; events can change the closest available route.
cylburn-mansion.hours: The current August 2026 facilities schedule lists Mansion hours Wednesday, Friday, Saturday and Sunday from 10:00 a.m.-2:00 p.m., with tours and activities on the second Saturday and Sunday. Recheck before visiting because building hours change separately from outdoor grounds.
cylburn-mansion.restrooms: Do not rely on Mansion restrooms outside staffed hours. The Greenhouse Classroom is the documented restroom location during general arboretum hours, with other building facilities available only when those buildings are open.
cylburn-mansion.fees: Viewing the Mansion exterior and ordinary arboretum grounds is free. Guided tours, rentals, programs, events and permitted photography can have separate arrangements or charges.
cylburn-mansion.accessibility: A paved route connects the upper parking area and Mansion zone, but historic thresholds, room access and event layouts can vary. Contact the operator before relying on a specific interior accommodation.
cylburn-mansion.dogs: Leashed dogs may use the outdoor grounds but should not be expected inside the Mansion. Service-animal access follows current building rules.
cylburn-mansion.family: The exterior and limited public hours can make a short history stop, but children must remain supervised around historic interiors, steps, furnishings and event setups.
cylburn-mansion.need: The Mansion and arboretum do not share one schedule. Build the visit around current posted Mansion hours if going inside matters; the exterior landscape remains useful during ordinary grounds hours.

carrie-murray-nature-center.name: Carrie Murray Nature Center
carrie-murray-nature-center.description: Carrie Murray Nature Center is the park's year-round environmental-education hub, offering scheduled live-animal, preschool, camp, school, public and volunteer programs.
carrie-murray-nature-center.location: Navigate to 1901 Ridgetop Road and the named Nature Center, not the broad Windsor Mill Road park address. The building is a distinct destination within the wooded park.
carrie-murray-nature-center.parking: Use the small Nature Center arrival area on Ridgetop Road. Capacity and group-program traffic can vary, so confirm arrangements for a class, camp or large group before driving in.
carrie-murray-nature-center.hours: The City describes year-round programs but does not publish dependable daily drop-in hours on the current page. Call 410-396-0808 or check the current program catalog before making building entry or a live-animal visit the purpose of the trip.
carrie-murray-nature-center.restrooms: Building restroom access depends on the Nature Center being open for a program or public visit. Remote park trails do not provide a dependable substitute.
carrie-murray-nature-center.fees: The park is free to enter, while camps, field trips, preschool, registered programs and special activities may require registration or a fee.
carrie-murray-nature-center.accessibility: Use the exact Ridgetop Road facility address for the shortest developed approach. Contact the center for program-specific mobility, sensory or communication accommodations.
carrie-murray-nature-center.dogs: Do not bring pets into a live-animal education facility unless current rules explicitly allow them. Leashed-dog park access remains separate outside the center, and service animals follow applicable rules.
carrie-murray-nature-center.family: This is the strongest staffed family anchor in the park when a suitable program is running. Check age, registration, start time and indoor availability rather than assuming continuous drop-in exhibits.
carrie-murray-nature-center.need: The Nature Center is program-led, not an always-open visitor center. Confirm the exact activity before crossing the park, especially for live animals, restrooms or indoor shelter.

orianda-mansion.name: Orianda Mansion
orianda-mansion.description: Orianda Mansion, also mapped as Crimea Mansion, is the historic stone house at the center of the Crimea Estate landscape near Eagle Drive.
orianda-mansion.address: Eagle Drive, Gwynns Falls Leakin Park, Baltimore, MD 21229
orianda-mansion.location: Use the Eagle Drive/Crimea Estate entrance identified on the official Friends map. Orianda and the nearby Magnolia Grove are west of Winans Meadow and are not served by the I-70 trailhead approach.
orianda-mansion.parking: Follow current Eagle Drive signs and use only open legal spaces serving the Crimea Estate area. Do not block mansion, maintenance or event access, and do not assume the building has public drop-in parking.
orianda-mansion.hours: The exterior landscape follows ordinary daylight park use unless an event, maintenance activity or posted closure controls the estate. The historic building does not publish regular drop-in interior hours on the park map.
orianda-mansion.restrooms: There is no dependable public restroom at the Mansion. Plan around Carrie Murray Nature Center only when it is confirmed open, or use facilities before entering the park.
orianda-mansion.fees: Viewing the Mansion exterior during ordinary park access is free. Private events, programs, rentals or interior access are separate and may not be available to casual visitors.
orianda-mansion.accessibility: Eagle Drive provides a developed approach, while historic walks, grass, grades and building thresholds vary. Confirm event or interior access directly rather than inferring it from the outdoor route.
orianda-mansion.dogs: Leashed dogs may use ordinary outdoor park routes but should not enter the Mansion or a private event. Remove waste and keep pets away from planted areas.
orianda-mansion.family: The Mansion and Magnolia Grove make a compact outdoor history-and-landscape stop, but there is no guaranteed staffed interpretation, restroom or indoor shelter.
orianda-mansion.need: Treat Orianda as an exterior landmark unless an announced program specifically includes the building. Save the exact Eagle Drive route before entering the wooded park.

gwynns-falls-trail.name: Gwynns Falls Trail
gwynns-falls-trail.description: The Gwynns Falls Trail is the park's principal shared walking and bicycling route, linking wooded Leakin Park segments to the larger Baltimore trail system.
gwynns-falls-trail.location: This pin marks the geotagged photographed trail segment east of the Crimea and Winans Meadow area. Download the full 2024 trail map because the route continues well beyond this one point.
gwynns-falls-trail.parking: Choose an official trailhead based on the planned segment: I-70 Park and Ride is Trail Head 1, Winans Meadow is Trail Head 2 and Windsor Mill is Trail Head 3. Do not leave a vehicle at an unrelated estate or facility after its access closes.
gwynns-falls-trail.hours: Use the trail during daylight park hours. Flooding, fallen trees, ice, maintenance and events can affect individual segments even when another trailhead remains open.
gwynns-falls-trail.restrooms: There is no continuous restroom service along the trail. Confirm a staffed facility before relying on it and plan remote segments as having no facilities.
gwynns-falls-trail.fees: Walking and bicycling the public trail are free. Programs, rentals, transit and events are separate.
gwynns-falls-trail.accessibility: The main trail provides the park's most predictable firm route, but crossings, grades, debris, detours and connections vary. Review the selected segment rather than assuming the entire corridor is level.
gwynns-falls-trail.dogs: Leashed dogs may use the trail. Keep to one side, yield to other users, control dogs near cyclists and wildlife and remove waste.
gwynns-falls-trail.family: A short out-and-back from a named trailhead is easier to manage than an open-ended route. Carry water, keep children out of streams and roadways and set a turnaround time.
gwynns-falls-trail.need: This is a long connected route, not a short loop around the parent pin. Download the official map, choose a trailhead and save enough daylight and energy for the return.

magnolia-grove.name: Magnolia Grove
magnolia-grove.description: Magnolia Grove is a seasonal collection of saucer magnolias in the Crimea section near Orianda Mansion, most visually distinctive during its brief spring bloom.
magnolia-grove.address: Crimea Estate, Gwynns Falls Leakin Park, Baltimore, MD 21229
magnolia-grove.location: Use the geotagged grove point near Orianda Mansion and approach through the Eagle Drive/Crimea Estate area. The official park map is still useful for the final walk.
magnolia-grove.parking: Use an open legal space serving the Eagle Drive/Crimea Estate area, then walk. Keep vehicles off lawns and planted areas and leave event and maintenance access clear.
magnolia-grove.hours: The outdoor grove follows daylight park access unless an event or posted closure controls the area. Bloom timing depends on winter and spring weather and cannot be guaranteed for a calendar date.
magnolia-grove.restrooms: There is no dependable public restroom at the grove or Mansion. Use facilities before arriving or confirm a staffed park building separately.
magnolia-grove.fees: Ordinary outdoor access is free. Permitted events or programs are separate.
magnolia-grove.accessibility: The final approach includes an outdoor estate landscape with grass, natural grades and weather-sensitive footing. The geotag reduces searching but does not guarantee a fully paved route.
magnolia-grove.dogs: Leashed dogs may accompany visitors outdoors. Keep them out of flower beds and away from private events, and remove waste.
magnolia-grove.family: The grove can be a memorable short seasonal stop paired with the Mansion exterior, but it has no play equipment, staffed interpretation or dependable facilities.
magnolia-grove.need: The published photograph shows full bloom in early April 2025, not a permanent year-round condition. Check recent local updates before making flowers the sole reason for the trip.

i-70-park-and-ride-trailhead.name: I-70 Park and Ride Trailhead
i-70-park-and-ride-trailhead.description: The former I-70 park-and-ride at the highway's eastern end is the official Friends map's Trail Head 1 and a practical western start for the park trail network.
i-70-park-and-ride-trailhead.address: I-70 Park and Ride, Baltimore, MD 21229
i-70-park-and-ride-trailhead.location: Navigate to the geotagged I-70 Park and Ride at the eastern highway terminus. This is Trail Head 1; it is west of the Eagle Drive estate area and far from Carrie Murray Nature Center.
i-70-park-and-ride-trailhead.parking: Use only the designated open park-and-ride area and obey current roadway, lot and overnight-parking signs. Secure the vehicle, take valuables and do not use highway shoulders as overflow parking.
i-70-park-and-ride-trailhead.hours: Begin and finish during daylight park hours. Lot restrictions, construction, police activity, events, snow or maintenance can affect access independently from the trail network.
i-70-park-and-ride-trailhead.restrooms: Do not expect a public restroom or water source at the park-and-ride. Prepare before arrival and carry water for the planned route.
i-70-park-and-ride-trailhead.fees: Ordinary trailhead parking and park access are free unless current signs state otherwise. Transit, events and programs are separate.
i-70-park-and-ride-trailhead.accessibility: The large paved arrival area is easier than many woodland entrances, but the onward trail surface, crossings, grades and current barriers must be assessed for the selected route.
i-70-park-and-ride-trailhead.dogs: Leashed dogs may start here for park trails. Keep them controlled in the parking area and near cyclists, and carry out waste.
i-70-park-and-ride-trailhead.family: The spacious arrival can simplify a short family trail outing, but there are no staffed facilities. Set a turnaround point, carry water and keep children close around vehicles and trail crossings.
i-70-park-and-ride-trailhead.need: This is an arrival point, not a full-service visitor center. Download the 2024 park map before leaving signal coverage and confirm that Trail Head 1 serves the route you actually want.
